title: C# Questions & Answers - Multithreaded Programming - 2
sourceFile: C# Questions & Answers - Multithreaded Programming - 2 - Sanfoundry.html
description: This set of C# Questions and Answers focuses on "Multithreaded Programming II".

questions.question: Which keyword is used for using the synchronization features defined by the Monitor class?
questions.explanation: lock (obj) { } is compiler sugar for Monitor.Enter/Exit (with a try/finally). Java's synchronized is not a C# keyword.

questions.question: What is synchronization in reference to a thread?

options.text: It's a process of handling situations when two or more threads need access to a shared resource
It's a process by which many threads are able to access the same shared resource simultaneously
It's a process by which a method is able to access many different threads simultaneously
It's a method that allows too many threads to access any information they require

questions.explanation: Synchronization coordinates threads so that a shared resource is used safely (often one thread at a time for a mutex, or a limited count for a semaphore). It is not "everyone accesses it at once".

questions.question: Which method is called when a thread is blocked from running temporarily?
questions.explanation: Monitor.Wait(obj) releases the lock and waits. Pulse/PulseAll wake waiters; they do not put the caller to sleep.

questions.question: What kind of exception is being thrown if Wait(), Pulse() or PulseAll() is called from code that is not within synchronized code?
questions.explanation: Monitor.Wait, Pulse, and PulseAll require the calling thread to own the monitor. Otherwise they throw SynchronizationLockException.

questions.question: What is mutex?

options.text: can be acquired by more than one thread at a time
helps in sharing of resource which can be used by one thread

questions.explanation: A mutex (System.Threading.Mutex, or lock/Monitor) can be owned by only one thread at a time. Option b is the opposite. Option c is roughly true but poorly worded; a is the definition. d is false because of b.

questions.question: What is Semaphore?

options.text: Grant more than one thread access to a shared resource at the same time
Useful when a collection of resources is being synchronized
Make use of a counter to control access to a shared resource

questions.explanation: A semaphore counts available slots. If the count is greater than zero, another thread may enter; Wait decrements and Release increments. That allows a limited number of concurrent users.

questions.question: Which method is used to abort thread prior to it's normal execution?
questions.explanation: Thread.Abort() requested thread termination via ThreadAbortException. It is obsolete and unsafe; prefer cooperative cancellation (CancellationToken). Sleep pauses; Suspend is obsolete; there is no Terminate().

questions.question: Which of these statements is incorrect?

options.text: By multithreading CPU idle time is minimized, and we can take maximum use of it
By multitasking CPU idle time is minimized, and we can take maximum use of it
Two thread in Csharp can have same priority
A thread can exist only in two states, running and blocked

questions.explanation: A thread has more than two states (Unstarted, Running, WaitSleepJoin, Stopped, and others). Two threads may share a priority. a and b are informal but not the false statement being asked for.

questions.question: What is multithreaded programming?

options.text: It's a process in which two different processes run simultaneously
It's a process in which two or more parts of same process run simultaneously
It's a process in which many different process are able to access same information
It's a process in which a single process can access information from many sources

questions.explanation: Multithreading runs two or more threads in the same process. Running different processes is multiprocessing / process-based multitasking.
